title: Salaried Employee with HRA & 80C
summary: Rahul earns 12L, pays 3L rent, and invests 1.5L in PPF. Should he choose the old or new regime?
steps: Step 1: Calculate New Regime Tax. 12L - 75k standard deduction = 11.25L taxable.
Step 2: Calculate Old Regime Tax. 12L - 50k standard - 3L HRA (approx) - 1.5L 80C = 7L taxable.
Step 3: Compare. The old regime tax on 7L is significantly lower than the new regime tax on 11.25L.
conclusion: Despite the hype, the Old Regime saves Rahul more tax because his deductions are high.

title: Freelancer with 44ADA
summary: Priya earns 40L as a consultant. She opts for presumptive taxation under 44ADA.
steps: Step 1: Under 44ADA, only 50% of gross receipts are deemed as profit.
Step 3: She pays tax on 20L instead of 40L, without maintaining detailed books of account.
conclusion: 44ADA is a massive benefit for freelancers with high revenue and low expenses.

title: Senior Citizen with FD Interest
summary: Mr. Sharma (65) earns 8L pension and 2L FD interest.
steps: Step 1: Pension is taxed as salary (standard deduction applies).
Step 2: FD interest is taxed under 'Income from Other Sources'.
Step 3: He can claim 80TTB deduction up to 50,000 on the FD interest.
conclusion: Seniors get higher exemption limits on interest income compared to regular citizens.
